title: Case: National Office Supplies
text: National Office Supplies sells office equipment to businesses through regional sales offices. Head office wants a “performance culture” and standard reward practices across all offices. There are no written rating criteria for bonuses anywhere in the company.

London office (manager: Jeff). The most profitable office and the largest. Each month the top seller by volume receives £250. An annual bonus pot of about £3,000 goes mostly to the top seller; reps can lobby Jeff, who decides at his discretion, can withhold the bonus and has rolled over £500 to the next year. The pot exists “in lieu of” a London allowance. Customers have complained about hard selling, the office administrator is looking for another job, and one rep calls the system “a great motivator if all you care about is money”.

Scotland office (manager: Nicola). Mid-table results. The annual pot is split equally among the reps, and part goes unofficially to the administrator. The team works remotely; Nicola is described as a “great boss” who keeps regular contact, recognises good work and organises get-togethers. One rep says the overall pay package trails competitors, although pay is “pretty good”.
Head office is considering rolling out the London model to all offices.
